records.reason: m11 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 34.6/101.0 mL. After efd84dffe823b6298db6 measured 37.6/118.0 at 150 uL with a historical V2 underprediction of 72.3 mL, this loading contrast tests whether the broad finish persists and whether onset changes independently.

m11 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 9.8/19.4 mL. Together with measured 10/1 record 6b5982c6e1bbaadd6a95 and the new 50/1 point, it constrains the oxime response before the sharp increase seen at 20/1 and 50/1.

m206 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 21.0/43.8 mL. The 10/1 measurement b7cf293311f83700cd9a reached 55.8/113.2 and exposed a large historical underprediction. This stronger-mobile-phase point tests where the naphthylmethanol tail develops.

m146 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 33.9/67.2 mL. Its measured 10/1 point 23ef03f3e75e40b20095 reached 51.3/108.5. Measuring the intermediate solvent strength tests whether the newly learned late regime transfers along the condition curve.

The matched m146 2/1, 100 uL point is predicted at 11.2/25.4 mL. Holding sample and loading solvent conditions fixed against the selected 5/1 point tests the predicted steep transition and distinguishes a solvent threshold from a general scaffold offset.

m178 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 19.0/51.1 mL, only slightly above measured 20/1 record 855456da9ea892f7216b at 18.8/48.9. This tests the predicted plateau after a major historical transfer failure, rather than assuming continued growth with increasing PE.

m59 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 38.4/74.4 mL, whereas its measured 1/1 anchor 19bdb9c6c59639662992 was 4.6/8.6. This tests an uncovered large solvent response for a flexible ether-containing aldehyde and can inform related oxygenated carbonyl rows.

Novel m205 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 17.4/39.4 mL. It tests transfer to a naphthylethanol after the large m206 failure at b7cf293311f83700cd9a. Linker length, ring attachment and loading volume differ, so the comparison teaches conditional graph transfer rather than isolating one substitution.

Novel m119 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 23.5/41.2 mL. Its methoxyphenethyl alcohol environment connects the measured primary-alcohol response of m204 with the aromatic alcohol failures, testing whether an additional ether changes onset and finish in a transferable way.

Novel secondary alcohol m60 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 18.1/30.8 mL. This probes hydroxyl placement and substitution between the covered primary alcohol m204 and tertiary alcohol m51, without presuming that all alcohols share their retention curve.

Novel ortho-isopropylphenol m58 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 9.5/16.6 mL and has low similarity to measured molecules. It supplies the stronger-eluent anchor for testing whether steric surroundings of a phenolic OH alter transfer from measured alcohol and phenol families.

The matched m58 50/1, 100 uL point is predicted at 26.3/47.3 mL. Its contrast with the selected 5/1 point isolates mobile-phase composition within this new scaffold and tests whether the model captures a hindered phenol's solvent sensitivity.

Novel meta-amino ester m88 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 11.4/22.8 mL. Positional amino-nitrile differences were measured at ad833f34f6b91872362d and a60552f4d1a5ced4641f; this asks whether comparable graph sensitivity transfers to amino esters.

Para-amino ester m86 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 14.1/29.4 mL and extends its measured 2/1 anchor d7f5057912ffbf1231a3. It complements m88, while the differing loading masses and DCM volumes of 500 versus 200 uL prevent a purely positional interpretation.

Novel tertiary-amino acrylate m19 at 2/1, 50 uL is predicted to elute compactly at 5.8/8.9 mL. Silica interaction by its basic nitrogen is a chemical reason to test this low prediction; the label can distinguish a genuinely early base from missed functional-group transfer.

Novel pyridyl ketone m66 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 13.7/24.5 mL with low structural similarity to measured rows. It tests whether the basic-ring response learned from m211, m216 and the recent m146 failure transfers to a carbonyl-substituted pyridine.

Novel pyridyl ester m90 at 10/1, 100 uL is predicted at 17.6/32.2 mL. Alongside m66, this samples basic nitrogen in a different carbonyl environment, where measured azaaromatics span much larger retention differences than acceptor counts alone explain.

Novel para-methoxyacetophenone m115 at 10/1, 50 uL is predicted at 16.2/40.2 mL. It tests aromatic ether–ketone transfer near measured m39 and ortho-methoxy m127, whose high-ratio observations show that carbonyl context and interval shape cannot be inferred from oxygen counts alone.

Novel m106 at 10/1, 100 uL is predicted at 16.0/41.0 mL and lies far from labeled rows in the supplied feature space. Its flexible ether chain and trifluoromethyl aryl ketone test transfer beyond the densely covered simple aromatic ketones.

Novel methyl-substituted cyclic aryl ketone m63 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 15.4/34.3 mL. Low molecular similarity and high feature distance make this a useful test of ring geometry and carbonyl accessibility in a moderate-retention region.

Novel fluorenyl acetyl scaffold m38 at 10/1, 100 uL is predicted at 13.3/35.6 mL. This probes whether fused-ring graph context transfers from the measured naphthyl ketone family, including c2334ccf8e6788ac6ca2, without assuming similar late behavior.

Novel trifluoroethyl acrylate m17 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 15.2/29.7 mL. It tests the model's substantially stronger retention response than ordinary alkyl acrylates, adding a fluorinated ester environment with limited measured structural coverage.

Novel chloroiodobenzene m151 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 6.2/14.1 mL and has low maximum similarity to measured structures. This compact nonpolar control tests heavy-halogen graph transfer and balances the batch's many polar response transitions.

Novel hydroxy/methoxybenzaldehyde m117 at 1/1, 150 uL is predicted at 11.0/46.4 mL. The model predicts an unusually broad finish despite the EA-rich mobile phase. This is the first half of a matched test of that response shape.

The matched m117 5/1, 150 uL point is predicted at 8.6/25.3 mL, substantially earlier than its selected 1/1 prediction despite less EA. Two labels directly test this reversal; intramolecular hydrogen bonding is a possible structural prior, not an established explanation.

Novel ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 at 10/1, 100 uL is predicted at 15.5/31.3 mL. Paired with the selected para isomer, it tests the large predicted positional difference. The different DCM loading volumes must remain part of the interpretation.

Para-nitrobenzaldehyde m193 at 10/1, 100 uL is predicted at 31.6/65.9 mL. Its measured 2/1 anchor f64ebc218e6ab29d7edc was 7.4/16.9. This anchors the predicted strong solvent response and makes the new ortho-isomer label more informative.

Novel bromosalicylaldehyde regioisomer m190 at 50/1, 100 uL is predicted at 8.4/27.5 mL. Measured m186 record 2efa93ea474f798b712a gives a nearby structural reference at 5.1/25.8; the DCM loading-volume difference, 300 versus 800 uL, is an explicit confound.

m173 at 10/1 with 1500 uL DCM loading solvent is predicted at 20.9/92.0 mL. It changes mobile-phase strength from measured 5/1 record 1e971da91b3a8229f0e0 while retaining the loading conditions, testing acid-specific onset/finish growth.

m164 in pure EA is predicted at 7.7/58.6 mL, whereas measured 20/1 record b7fffd840d208b29776c finished at 35.7 mL. This tests a surprising stronger-eluent extrapolation for a donorless conjugated ketone and can correct a broad-finish artifact if unsupported.

Novel fused oxygen-containing aldehyde m194 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 11.8/23.8 mL. Its low similarity adds a targeted graph-transfer test connecting the selected flexible oxygenated aldehyde m59 with the covered aromatic ether/carbonyl families.

m28 at 5/1, 100 uL is predicted at 26.0/57.2 mL. The same loading at 10/1 was measured at 39.1/81.4 in 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a. This stronger-eluent point constrains a steep multifunctional-carbonyl response between the existing low- and high-ratio observations.

hypotheses.content: Large late-elution losses arise from scaffold-specific solvent-response transitions. After learning a late point, the model may still misplace the transition or transfer its onset and finish incorrectly to stronger mobile phases.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest recent historical errors occurred in distinct late regimes, while some intermediate-condition predictions were already accurate. Labels on unresolved parts of these curves can teach conditional response shape rather than only a molecule-level offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m146 at 2/1 and 5/1, m206 at 5/1, and the m11 and m28 intermediate points show the predicted transition locations? Does m178 actually plateau between 20/1 and 50/1?

hypotheses.content: In several measured families, increased sample loading advances V1 more than it changes V2. This provisional pattern is scaffold-dependent, and the predictor's nearly invariant loading predictions may miss it.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separating onset movement from finish movement can improve both targets across repeated condition rows. The m211 contrast warns that a shared directional loading rule could also introduce errors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m11 50/1, does the 100 uL measurement preserve the very broad finish measured at 150 uL, and how much does its onset change?

hypotheses.content: Graph context and functional-group surroundings affect retention and solvent sensitivity beyond coarse donor/acceptor counts. Accessibility, basic-site environment and intramolecular interactions are plausible contributors, but their mechanisms are not established by these labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched amino-nitrile isomers differ at both measured loadings, and recent scaffold additions exposed large transfer errors. Related new structures can teach useful graph distinctions while ordinary and compact examples constrain overgeneralization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which distinctions transfer to amino esters, pyridyl carbonyls, differently substituted hydroxyl groups and oxygenated aromatic carbonyls after accounting for their recorded loading conditions?

hypotheses.content: Broad finishes under EA-rich conditions and nonmonotonic solvent-response predictions require molecule-specific testing. Some broad intervals are measured, but others have been prediction artifacts; neither broadness nor an assumed monotonic rule is sufficient evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The acid retained a broad measured interval in pure EA, whereas the multifunctional m13 pure-EA finish had been strongly overpredicted. Discriminating these cases can prevent unsupported tails from propagating into common stronger-eluent rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does matched m117 really finish much later at 1/1 than at 5/1, and does donorless m164 sustain its predicted broad interval in pure EA?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes shift emphasis away from further loading interpolation in well-covered m204 and m107 neighborhoods. Their newest points were mostly within roughly 1–6 mL per endpoint, and m160 at fe66b2381d33aa2ea3a8 was also accurate at acquisition. In contrast, m11 at efd84dffe823b6298db6, m146 at 23ef03f3e75e40b20095, and m206 at b7cf293311f83700cd9a had historical V2 underpredictions of 72.3, 54.2 and 44.4 mL. These motivate unresolved condition curves and related new scaffolds. Errors remain bidirectional: m13 at 1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23 and m26 at fa851bcd2cdb1d84b91f had V2 overpredictions near 26 mL. The m13 10/1 loading contrast also changed onset substantially while leaving finish similar. Thus a universal polar broad-tail rule remains unsupported; m13 itself has no H-bond donor. Accurate compact p-xylene and dibenzyl-ether outcomes support retaining a small ordinary-transfer check. Finally, the close m173 1500/2000 uL results reduce the value of another fine loading-solvent-volume contrast, so its selected follow-up changes mobile-phase composition instead. These errors are acquisition-time feedback, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines repair of consequential failure regions with tests of whether those repairs generalize. m146, m58 and m117 provide interpretable within-molecule solvent comparisons; m11 supplies a focused loading contrast plus an intermediate solvent anchor. m206, m178, m59, m173 and m28 constrain unresolved curve shapes without repeatedly sampling already well-characterized m204/m107 conditions. New alcohol, phenol, basic nitrogen, amino ester and carbonyl environments target the kinds of structural transfer that recently failed, while the compact chloroiodobenzene point checks against spreading late-retention corrections too broadly. Feature distance and quantile widths help identify gaps but are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Cross-molecule comparisons retain their loading-mass, solvent and loading-volume differences explicitly. Measuring both endpoints across these relationships should improve interpolation and graph-condition transfer over the Row-distribution, rather than merely increasing the number of extreme labels.
